title: Distribution Shift Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery using Machine Learning Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.13510v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Remote sensing imagery acquired by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) supports wide range of applications; however, deploying machine learning (ML) models on resource-constrained aerial platforms introduces challenges beyond predictive accuracy, particularly when deployment data differ from the distributions observed during training. Such shifts are common in remote sensing due to geographic, sensor, seasonal, and other visual variations. A practical solution is to equip deployed models with mechanisms that detect emerging distribution shifts and support subsequent responsive actions. This paper presents an empirical case study of three open-source detection tools: (i) Alibi-Detect; (ii) NannyML; and (iii) PyTorch-OOD. translated_title: 基于机器学习模型的遥感影像分布偏移检测
translated_abstract: 由无人机（UAV）获取的遥感影像支持广泛的应用；然而，在资源受限的航空平台上部署机器学习（ML）模型会带来超出预测准确性之外的挑战，尤其是当部署时的数据与训练期间观察到的分布不同时。由于地理、传感器、季节及其他视觉变化，这类分布偏移在遥感领域十分常见。一种实用的解决方案是为已部署的模型配备能够检测新出现分布偏移的机制，并支持后续的响应行动。本文对三种开源检测工具进行了实证案例研究：(i) Alibi-Detect；(ii) NannyML；(iii) PyTorch-OOD。基于跨数据集的遥感偏移场景，我们评估了这些工具的检测有效性和计算延迟。我们的结果揭示了不同方法及实现在检测行为和处理成本方面的差异……
tldr: 本文针对无人机遥感影像场景，实证评估了Alibi-Detect、NannyML和PyTorch-OOD三种开源分布偏移检测工具在跨数据集偏移下的检测有效性与计算延迟。
en_tdlr: This paper empirically evaluates three open-source distribution shift detection tools—Alibi-Detect, NannyML, and PyTorch-OOD—for remote sensing imagery, comparing their detection effectiveness and computational latency under cross-dataset shifts.
